method: aii-web-tools: 10 dated queries (3 scholarly via OpenAlex, 7 general) plus regex greps of 4 arXiv abstract pages, all run 2026-10-25T00:57Z; raw outputs in results/positioning_raw.json. Quotes below are copied verbatim from those raw outputs; where only a title was retrieved, the title is the quote and the entry says so.
deviation: run at elapsed 7.2 h (planned 2:00-3:30) because of the container crash; after commit #1, so any heuristic found here is descriptive only and does not join the corpus

sources.quote: We introduce DENIAL PROMPTING which pushes LLMs to develop more creative solutions to a given problem by incrementally imposing new constraints on the previous solution, compelling LLMs to adopt new strategies.
sources.why: Closest prior work: it bans techniques in code generation and scores creativity, but it does not set a lexical (name-based) compliance reading against an exact behavioural reading of the same program, which is the gap this artifact measures.

sources.quote: real-world applications often demand stricter adherence to detailed requirements such as coding style, line count, and structural constraints, beyond mere correctness.
sources.why: Checks instruction constraints in code with programmatic checks, but on style and structure constraints, not on prohibitions of a named algorithm read through behaviour.

sources.id: arXiv:2510.27353 (Herrmann and Pallez, An In-depth Study of LLM Contributions to the Bin Packing Problem)
sources.quote: we reassess this claim through a detailed analysis of the heuristics produced by LLMs, examining both their behavior and interpretability.
sources.quote_2: The derived algorithms are significantly simpler, more efficient, more interpretable, and more generalizable, suggesting that the considered instances are themselves relatively simple.
sources.why: Behavioural analysis of LLM-evolved bin-packing heuristics; supplies the ab family used here as the 'simple baseline' corpus. No prohibition or compliance study.

sources.id: arXiv:2407.10873 (Zhang et al., Understanding the Importance of Evolutionary Search in Automated Heuristic Design with LLMs)
sources.quote: inconsistent benchmark settings, inadequate baselines, and a lack of detailed component analysis have left the necessity of integrating LLMs with search strategies
sources.why: Compares LLM sampling with evolutionary program search on AHD problems including bin packing; relevant to the one-shot (no search) setting used here, not to compliance.

sources.id: arXiv:2603.02787 (ICLR 2026, Rethinking Code Similarity for Automated Algorithm Design with LLMs; BehaveSim)
sources.quote: Rethinking Code Similarity for Automated Algorithm Design with LLMs
sources.quote_note: title only (abstract not fetched in the time left)
sources.why: Behaviour-based similarity of generated heuristics, the convention this artifact follows with exact decision agreement on committed probe states.

sources.quote: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
sources.why: Source of the priority(item, bins) harness, the OR3 / Weibull 5k test sets and the c12/c14 heuristics in the corpus.

sources.quote: Evolution of Heuristics: Towards Efficient Automatic Algorithm Design Using Large Language Model
sources.why: Its final populations are corpus members (novelty reference).

sources.id: arXiv:2501.11411 (Beyond the Hype: Benchmarking LLM-Evolved Heuristics for Bin Packing)
sources.quote: Beyond the Hype: Benchmarking LLM-Evolved Heuristics for Bin Packing
sources.why: Generalisation critique of LLM-evolved bin-packing heuristics; supports judging 'better' only on held-out families.

sources.id: arXiv:2510.03178 (When Names Disappear: Revealing What LLMs Actually Understand About Code)
sources.quote: When Names Disappear: Revealing What LLMs Actually Understand About Code
sources.why: Names versus semantics in code COMPREHENSION; the present question is the generation-side analogue (does a banned rule survive under another name).

sources.id: arXiv:2510.12047 (Do Large Language Models Respect Contracts? Contract-Adherence in Code Generation)
sources.quote: Do Large Language Models Respect Contracts? Evaluating and Enforcing Contract-Adherence in Code Generation
sources.why: Adherence checked by execution rather than text, for contracts (pre/postconditions), not for algorithm prohibitions.

sources.id: arXiv:2608.07614 (DevIntent: How Much Does LLM-Generated Code Violate Developer Intent?)
sources.quote: DevIntent: How Much Does LLM-Generated Code Violate Developer Intent?
sources.why: Intent violation in generated code (2026); not about named-algorithm bans or behavioural equivalence classes.
The dated query 'counter-intuitive constraints code generation LLM fail 2026' did not return it; the plan's figure is cited from the strategy's reading and is NOT verified here.
Its seed function is a corpus member (ext/ files pinned in inputs/bp9/ext_sources.json).

overall: No source found by these queries OCCUPIES the question (lexical versus exact-behaviour compliance with named-algorithm bans in generated code). The nearest work is denial prompting (NeoCoder), which imposes technique bans for creativity scoring; IFEvalCode and contract-adherence work check constraints in code but not algorithm identity under renaming.
